learning_outcomes.text: Students master the fundamentals and laws for calculating currents and voltages in electrical DC and AC circuits.
They are able to analyze, mathematically describe, and transform electrical networks.
They have understood the basics of complex AC calculation and can apply them to practical examples.

syllabus_topics: Linear DC circuits: reference directions; current and voltage sources; Kirchhoff's equations; simple resistance networks (voltage divider, current divider); real current and voltage sources; interactions between source and load (interconnection of voltage sources, power matching, efficiency); superposition principle; analysis of extensive networks.

Transition to time-dependent current and voltage forms: overview and introduction of various characteristic quantities (average value, rectified value, RMS value, maximum value, peak value, peak-to-peak value, amplitude).

Alternating current and alternating voltage: the phasor diagram; complex AC calculation; description of concentrated RLC components and ideal sources; introduction of locus curves; calculation of simple AC circuits via the complex plane; energy and power in AC voltage; power matching.
Analysis of networks: mesh current method; nodal potential method.

Introduction to two-ports: port condition; two-port equations in matrix form (impedance, admittance, hybrid, chain form); two-port properties (reciprocity, symmetry); matrices of elementary two-ports.
assessment_rules: Credits are awarded upon successful completion of the module exam.
